slides.title: Periodontium
bullets: The tissues that support the tooth

slides.title: What Is the Periodontium?
bullets: The complex of tissues that surround and support the tooth
Gingiva, alveolar bone, periodontal ligament and root cementum
slides.caption: Tooth cross-section

slides.title: Components of the Periodontium
bullets: Gingiva — the soft tissue that covers the area around the neck of the tooth
Alveolar bone — the part of the jawbone that forms the socket holding the tooth root
Periodontal ligament — connects the tooth to the bone
Cementum — the root surface, where the ligament fibers attach

slides.title: How the Tooth Is Held Firmly
bullets: Ligament fibers attach to cementum at one end and to bone at the other
They help distribute chewing forces evenly to the bone
slides.caption: The roots sit within the jawbone

slides.title: Gingivitis and Periodontitis
bullets: Gingivitis — inflammation of the gingiva; it can reverse with proper hygiene and treatment
Periodontitis — inflammation that has spread to the tooth-supporting tissues, including bone
Signs: red, bleeding gums; a definitive diagnosis comes from a dentist

slides.title: Key Points
bullets: The ligament attaches the tooth to the bone
Bleeding gums are a reason to see a dentist

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the periodontium?
quiz.explanation: Enamel is a layer of the crown; the periodontium is the tissue that supports the tooth.

quiz.q: To which root layer do the ligament fibers attach?

quiz.explanation: Gingivitis is inflammation of the gingiva.

quiz.q: How does periodontitis differ from gingivitis?
options: The supporting tissues, including bone, are damaged
There is no difference at all
quiz.explanation: In periodontitis, the supporting tissues are damaged.

quiz.q: What should be done if the gums bleed?
quiz.explanation: The exact cause and treatment are determined by a dentist.
